title: GPU Budget Advisor: telemetry-driven KV reservation and eviction cost model for continuous batching
creator: Maya K. Patel
description: Background: Continuous batching plus large per-request KV caches cause non-linear GPU memory pressure spikes that we currently mitigate with static heuristics and blunt eviction. Those heuristics either waste GPU headroom or trigger costly preempts and SLO regressions for high-priority tenants. Goal: Design and implement a GPU Budget Advisor service (runtime-side controller + rollout plan) that uses telemetry to produce per-node/per-pool suggestions for: 1) weight/KV/activation soft budget splits, 2) safe headroom targets at configurable percentiles, and 3) an eviction cost model that ranks KV entries by expected SLO impact when evicted. The Advisor should produce actionable configs for the serving runtime and an operator-facing dashboard. Scope: - Prototype controller that ingests memory telemetry (allocations, active KV size distribution, sequence-length histograms, continuous-batch sizes, preempt events) and outputs budget recommendations. - Implement an eviction scoring function in the runtime that uses advisor-provided weights (age, last-access, sequence-length correlation, model layer hotspot, tenant priority). - A/B rollout plan for gradual adoption on a single Dedicated pool. Out of scope: changing model weights placement, work on quantization, or tenant billing changes. Constraints: - Minimal added tail latency overhead (<1ms p50 per-request). - No per-request remote calls to the Advisor (advisor outputs cached per-node policies). - Safety: advisor recommendations must be guarded by conservative default caps and a manual rollback knob.
acceptance_criteria: Advisor produces per-pool recommended memory split (weights/KV/activations) and recommended headroom percentiles (P50/P90/P99) via API and writes to runtime config store.

Serving runtime applies eviction score produced using advisor weights and demonstrably reduces high-priority SLO breaches during KV pressure experiments compared to baseline eviction (charted in experiment notebook).
End-to-end experiment shows at least 12% reduction in costly preempts or OOMs for target pool under mixed sequence-length load with equivalent p50 latency.
Operator dashboard shows advisor recommendations, rationale, recent telemetry signals (KV-hit-rate, KV-size-percentiles, active-batches) and decision timestamps.
Rollout plan documented with canary > 10% > 50% > full and automated rollback on error budget spike.
Code merged: controller, runtime eviction hook, and unit/integration tests.

notes: Advisor algorithm idea: combine time-decayed access frequency, last-seen sequence-length correlation, and a predicted eviction-penalty model derived from historical SLO violations when similar KV entries were removed.
Memory split starting suggestion (initial conservative defaults): weights=70%, KV=18%, activations=10% for N=2k average seq length pools; advisor will adjust per-pool.
Fallback policy: if advisor data is stale > 10m, revert to operator-configured static policy and alert.
